Let \(P(H)=\frac23\) and \(P(T)=\frac13\), since heads are twice as likely as tails.

For 8 flips, the probability of getting exactly \(k\) heads is

\[
\binom{8}{k}\left(\frac23\right)^k\left(\frac13\right)^{8-k}.
\]

We want the ratio

\[
\frac{P(\text{exactly 3 heads})}{P(\text{exactly 2 heads})}.
\]

So,

\[
\frac{\binom{8}{3}\left(\frac23\right)^3\left(\frac13\right)^5}
{\binom{8}{2}\left(\frac23\right)^2\left(\frac13\right)^6}
\]

\[
= \frac{\binom{8}{3}}{\binom{8}{2}}
\cdot \frac{\left(\frac23\right)^3}{\left(\frac23\right)^2}
\cdot \frac{\left(\frac13\right)^5}{\left(\frac13\right)^6}
\]

\[
= 2 \cdot \frac23 \cdot 3
\]

\[
= 4.
\]

So Phillip is \(4\) times as likely to get exactly three heads as exactly two heads.

The answer is 4.
